signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/SEK trades at 9.747, positioned above its SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200 cluster (SMA20 at 9.564). The G10 currency strength scorecard flags USD as the top performer with a +0.600% average gain across 9 pairs, while SEK is the primary laggard at −0.701% across 2 pairs, generating a 1.301% leader-to-laggard spread. Fed policy at 3.75% versus Riksbank at 1.75% provides a +200bp carry advantage that continues to anchor the divergence. Economic data underpins this split: the US Economic Surprise Index sits neutral at 0.0, whereas Sweden's ESI shows persistent weakness at −29.2. BEER-model valuation confirms the stretch, with USD/SEK trading rich at z=+1.67σ. Trade bias: Bullish USD/SEK; broad G10 outperformance and macroeconomic divergence support continued upside. Catalyst: US Retail Sales release at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Leader-to-laggard spread compresses below 0.80%, signaling a broader unwind of the bilateral trend.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Risk Reversals
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.93, holding below its SMA20/50/200 moving-average cluster (SMA20 at 157.36). SOFR at 3.62% against TONA at 0.98% generates a +264bp OIS carry differential favoring the dollar, maintaining baseline yield support. However, options pricing reflects strong downside hedging, with 1M 25d risk reversals printed at −1.95 (put skew), while CFTC positioning reveals Leveraged Funds net short −53,255 contracts despite a WoW short-covering add of +58,042. Geopolitical headlines regarding a proposed Strait of Hormuz oil truce add headline sensitivity without triggering safe-haven flows, as VIX remains contained at 17.1. Trade bias: Neutral/cautious USD/JPY; substantial OIS carry support is counterbalanced by heavy downside options hedging and technical resistance. Catalyst: Fed Interest Rate Decision and FOMC statement on 16 September. Risk: A sustained breakout above the SMA20 at 157.36 forces short-covering and invalidates downside skew protection.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Retail Extreme Divergence + Carry
signals.text: EUR/CHF trades at 0.9425, holding below its 20-day SMA. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment displays an extreme 88% net-short bias, contrasting with CFTC institutional data where CHF spec positioning sits heavily net short at −13,968 contracts (pctl 12, z −1.09). ECB policy at 2.65% against SNB at 0.00% creates a +265bp carry differential in favor of the euro, which is reinforced by Switzerland's negative real policy rate of −1.24% versus the Eurozone's +0.31%. Retail traders are aggressively fading this positive carry advantage, creating a setup for a contrarian squeeze higher if euro support holds. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/CHF; structural carry advantage and extreme retail short positioning favor upside mean-reversion. Catalyst: SNB Interest Rate Decision on 24 September. Risk: Broad European risk aversion forces safe-haven CHF inflows that overpower the yield differential.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Rates Neutrality + Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3468, holding between its SMA50 (1.3481) and SMA200 (1.3454). Policy rates for both the Fed and the Bank of England sit tied at 3.75%, resulting in a minimal −11bp OIS SONIA-SOFR spread that leaves the pair devoid of clear carry momentum. ATM 1M implied volatility trades at 5.4% against a 30-day realized volatility of 3.7%, driving a +1.7% Volatility Risk Premium as options markets price in elevated event risk. Meanwhile, UK labour market data shows cooling payrolls alongside wage growth deceleration, reducing pressure for near-term BoE tightening. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; balanced rate differentials and moving-average compression favor range-bound price action. Catalyst: UK CPI release at 06:00 UTC on 16 September. Risk: A sharp breakout beyond the SMA50/SMA200 bounds (1.3454–1.3481) forces systematic trend-following participation.
